request.name: CISO: .codx task JSONs are tracked in git — guard_diff blocks every repo-wide change (1401 findings)
request.description:
STRUCTURAL FINDING (reproduced twice: shift 2026-11-17 and shift 2026-11-18)
`security_review_changes(scope="unstaged")` → decision=block, highest_severity=critical, risk_score≈4379, 1401 findings, essentially all `secret.high-entropy-token` inside `.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/<task>.json` (e.g. `.codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog/codx-junior-website-requests.7bc1d585-…json` lines 15005-15181). One earlier run flagged 263/269 findings from a single +4897-line task log.

WHY IT MATTERS
- The control plane (`.codx/`: task bodies, chat turns, tool output, model replies) is stored in the git working tree and therefore enters every diff the security gate inspects. The gate therefore returns `block` for the whole repository on churn that nobody intends to commit, and the real signal (a genuine secret in code) is buried under ~1400 false positives.
- Worse, it is the exact channel that leaked credentials before: model/tool output is persisted verbatim into task JSONs, and those files are one `git add -A` away from being committed. `.gitignore` could not be read through the project tools (.gitignore at repo root is outside the wiki root), so the tracking status itself must be confirmed by the owner.

WHAT TO DO (owner: repository / devops)
1. `git ls-files .codx | head` — confirm whether `.codx` is tracked. If it is tracked: stop tracking it (`git rm -r --cached .codx`) and add `.codx/` to the repo-root `.gitignore`, keeping only the deliberate, non-sensitive parts if any are needed.
2. If parts must stay tracked (profiles, boards definitions), split them: keep declarative config tracked and exclude task/chat/session payloads.
3. Until then, document the workaround for reviewers: always scope the gate (`security_review_changes(scope="staged")`, or a `paths` filter) and never treat an unscoped `block` as a code finding.
4. Consider adding `.codx` to `security_policy.ignore_paths` ONLY after the tracking decision is made — silencing the path while it is still committable would hide real leaks.

ACCEPTANCE
- `security_review_changes(scope="unstaged")` returns fewer than 20 findings, none of them inside `.codx/`.
- `git status --porcelain` after a normal agent shift shows no `.codx/tasks/**` entries.
- A comment on this card quotes both commands' output before and after.
